---
title: "Freud CLI Reference"
---

This page is a quick reference for the `freud` command-line tool: how to invoke it, what flags it accepts, and how each feature should behave.

For how to **implement** a new feature, see [First Steps](../Getting-Started/First-Steps.qmd) and [Workflows & Milestones](../ProjectManagement/Workflows.qmd).

---

## Basic usage

```bash
./freud.exe -f <image> -c <command>
```

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `-f <path>` | Input image path. Can be repeated for commands that take multiple images. |
| `-c <command>` | Feature to run. Must match an entry in `freud.manifest`. |
| `-o <path>` | Output image path. Default: `image_out.bmp` |
| `--debug` | Print debug information (image loaded, dimensions, etc.) |
| `--version` | Print version and exit |

---

## Example invocations

```bash
# Print image dimensions
./freud.exe -f images/input/image.jpeg -c dimension

# Make the image red
./freud.exe -f images/input/image.jpeg -c color_red

# Rotate clockwise and save with custom name
./freud.exe -f images/input/image.jpeg -c rotate_cw -o rotated.bmp

# Debug mode (prints image info before running)
./freud.exe --debug -f images/input/image.jpeg -c dimension
```

## Feature index

### Milestone 1 — Tutorial

| Command | Output |
|---|---|
| `helloworld` | Prints `Hello World!` |
| `dimension` | `dimension: <width>, <height>` |
| `color_first_pixel` | `color_first_pixel: R, G, B` |
| `color_10th_pixel` | `color_10th_pixel: R, G, B` |
| `color_first_pixel_second_line` | `color_first_pixel_second_line: R, G, B` |
| `pixelRGB` | Uses `pixelRGB` struct, get and print functions |

### Milestone 2 — Statistics

| Command | Output |
|---|---|
| `max_pixel` | `max_pixel (x, y): R, G, B` |
| `min_pixel` | `min_pixel (x, y): R, G, B` |
| `max_component` | `max_component: value` |
| `min_component` | `min_component: value` |
| `full_report` | Writes a `.txt` file with all statistics |

### Milestone 3 — Colors

| Command | Output |
|---|---|
| `color_red` | Image with only red channel kept |
| `color_green` | Image with only green channel kept |
| `color_blue` | Image with only blue channel kept |
| `grayscale` | Grayscale via channel averaging |
| `invert` | Each channel inverted (255 − value) |
| `luminance` | Grayscale via luminance formula |
| `desaturate` | Desaturated image |

### Milestone 4 — Transforms

| Command | Output |
|---|---|
| `rotate_cw` | Image rotated 90° clockwise |
| `rotate_ccw` | Image rotated 90° counter-clockwise |
| `mirror_h` | Mirror effect — horizontal symmetry |
| `mirror_v` | Mirror effect — vertical symmetry |
| `mirror` | Mirror effect (combined) |
| `crop` | Cropped image |

### Milestone 5 — Resize

| Command | Output |
|---|---|
| `scale_nn` | Scale via nearest-neighbor interpolation |
| `scale_bilinear` | Scale via bilinear interpolation |

> **Note:** Check each feature's issue file in [Features](Features.qmd) for the exact expected output format. The CI compares output character by character — spacing and capitalization must match exactly.

## The manifest file

`freud.manifest` is a plain text file at the project root. It lists every command your binary supports, one per line:

```
helloworld
dimension
color_first_pixel
color_red
```

**Rules:**
- One command per line, no spaces, no quotes
- The CI reads this file to know which features to test
- If a command is implemented but missing from the manifest, the CI will not test it
- If a command is in the manifest but not implemented, the CI test will fail

---

## Adding a new feature — the pattern

Every new feature requires **four changes**:

### 1. Declare in `src/features.h`

```c
void my_feature(char *source_path);
```

### 2. Implement in `src/features.c`

```c
void my_feature(char *source_path) {
    unsigned char *data = NULL;
    int width, height, channels;
    read_image_data(source_path, &data, &width, &height, &channels);
    // ... your logic ...
    free(data);
}
```

### 3. Dispatch in `src/main.c`

```c
if (strcmp(conf.command, "my_feature") == 0) {
    my_feature(conf.filenames[0]);
}
```

### 4. Register in `freud.manifest`

```
my_feature
```

Miss any one of these four steps and the feature either won't compile, won't run, or won't be tested by the CI.

## The `Config` struct

`src/configp.h` defines the configuration parsed from command-line arguments:

```c
typedef struct _config {
    int    debug_mode;                       // --debug flag
    char   command[MAX_LENGTH_COMMAND];      // -c <command>
    char*  filenames[MAX_FILE_COUNT];        // -f <path> (can repeat)
    char*  arguments[MAX_ARGUMENT_COUNT];   // additional arguments
} Config;
```

`conf.filenames[0]` is the first `-f` argument — the input image path.

---

## Key library functions

From `estia-image/include/estia-image.h`:

```c
// Read image from file. Returns 0 on success.
int read_image_data(const char *filename,
                    unsigned char **data,
                    int *width, int *height, int *nbChannels);

// Write image to file. Returns 0 on success.
int write_image_data(const char *filename,
                     unsigned char *data,
                     int width, int height);
```

Pixel access pattern (RGB, 3 channels):

```c
int index = (y * width + x) * 3;
unsigned char R = data[index];
unsigned char G = data[index + 1];
unsigned char B = data[index + 2];
```

See [Image Data Structure](../Resources/Image-Data-Structure.qmd) for a full explanation of how pixels are laid out in memory.
